title: Voltpilot MQTT Device Data Purge
description: Device data purge ('Datenaufzeichnungen loeschen'): delete ALL recorded timeseries and OCPP recording data of one device without unclaiming it. Two messages on EXISTING topics (no ACL change): the edge durably records its cloud-purge intent before fallible local cleanup, then requests a purge on its own status topic (the broker's per-device ACL + mTLS cert identity make this an authenticated request for the device's OWN data); the cloud publishes the RETAINED purge_data command on the device's command topic after every purge - both portal- and device-initiated - so the device wipes its local store-and-forward buffer, live history and OCPP journal. The retained command reaches an offline device the moment it reconnects. Correctness never depends on the device cooperating: the cloud also stamps a purge watermark (device.data_purged_before) and the timescale-writer refuses any sample observed at or before it, so replayed old buffer entries can never resurrect purged history. This file is a BINDING contract like the other files in this directory; it is ADDITIVE - the frozen telemetry/schedule/provisioning contracts are unchanged.

x-topics.purge_request: ems/{tenant_id}/{site_id}/{device_id}/status  (Device -> Cloud, QoS1, not retained; the regular status heartbeats share this topic and carry no `type` field)
x-topics.purge_data: ems/{tenant_id}/{site_id}/{device_id}/command  (Cloud -> Edge, QoS1, RETAINED; re-published after every purge, cleared on unclaim)

x-semantics.identity: Topic identity MUST equal payload identity in both directions; the cloud additionally resolves the device row for the topic's tenant before purging (a fabricated identity resolves to nothing and is ignored).
x-semantics.device-side-ordering: For a local request the edge atomically persists purge-request.json with local_cleanup_pending BEFORE any fallible local deletion. Cleanup errors remain visible and are retried after restart; the original cloud request is re-sent on reconnect. On either local purge or purge_data the edge drops every locally buffered/recorded sample and OCPP journal event observed at or before the watermark BEFORE replay resumes. Corrupt, unreadable or timestamp-undecodable journal files are conservatively erased because they cannot safely be classified as newer. Samples/events known to be after the watermark are kept and upload normally.
x-semantics.cloud-concurrency: Cloud purge and OCPP ingest serialize on the same database-wide per-device lock. Ingest re-reads data_purged_before inside its transaction after acquiring that lock, so a post-watermark OCPP event commits journal plus all read models only after the sweep, while an at/before-watermark replay is atomically refused.
x-semantics.confirmation: The retained purge_data command doubles as the cloud's confirmation of a device-initiated purge: a device that requested a purge treats a purge_data with purged_before >= its request time as 'confirmed'.
x-semantics.offline-device: A portal purge against an offline device deletes the cloud data immediately; the retained command wipes the device's local buffers on its next reconnect. A device-initiated purge while offline wipes locally at once and (re-)publishes the purge_request on every reconnect until confirmed.
x-semantics.idempotent: Purging is idempotent on both sides: re-purging an already-empty device just advances the watermark.

ts.description: When the customer triggered the purge on the device (RFC 3339, UTC).

purged_before.description: The purge watermark: everything observed at or before this instant is deleted in the cloud, refused by the writer, and must be dropped from device-local buffers.
